source: Curated list of widely documented world events, one entry per date where available.
note: Dates are given in the Gregorian calendar. Matching uses the month and day only.

events.title: Australia becomes a federation
events.description: Six British colonies joined to form the Commonwealth of Australia.

events.title: Luna 9 lands on the Moon
events.description: The Soviet probe made the first soft landing on another world and sent back pictures from the surface.

events.title: Explorer 1 reaches orbit
events.description: The first American satellite discovered the Van Allen radiation belts around the Earth.

events.title: Space Shuttle Columbia is lost
events.description: The orbiter broke up during re-entry over Texas, killing all seven astronauts on board.

events.title: First scheduled Concorde tests
events.description: Supersonic passenger flight moved closer as the prototype programme expanded its test campaign.

events.title: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
events.description: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first people to walk on the lunar surface.

events.title: Viking 1 lands on Mars
events.description: The first fully successful landing on Mars returned photographs from the plains of Chryse.

events.title: Yuri Gagarin orbits the Earth
events.description: Vostok 1 carried the first human into space for a single orbit lasting 108 minutes.

events.title: First Space Shuttle launch
events.description: Columbia flew the first mission of the reusable Space Transportation System.

events.title: Hubble Space Telescope launched
events.description: Discovery carried the observatory that would reshape modern astronomy into orbit.

events.title: Sputnik 1 opens the space age
events.description: The Soviet Union launched the first artificial satellite of the Earth.

events.title: John Glenn orbits the Earth
events.description: Friendship 7 made him the first American to complete orbits of the planet.

events.title: Challenger disaster
events.description: The shuttle broke apart 73 seconds after launch, killing its crew of seven.

events.title: Mars Pathfinder lands
events.description: The mission delivered Sojourner, the first rover to drive on Mars.

events.title: Curiosity lands in Gale Crater
events.description: The car-sized rover touched down on Mars using a rocket-powered sky crane.

events.title: New Horizons flies past Pluto
events.description: The first close-up images revealed nitrogen glaciers and towering water-ice mountains.

events.title: First image of a black hole
events.description: The Event Horizon Telescope published its picture of the shadow of the black hole in M87.

events.title: Galileo sees Jupiter's moons
events.description: His telescope revealed the four large satellites now named after him.

events.title: Neptune discovered
events.description: Johann Galle found the planet within a degree of the position predicted by Le Verrier.

events.title: William Herschel discovers Uranus
events.description: The first planet found with a telescope doubled the known size of the Solar System.

events.title: Pluto discovered
events.description: Clyde Tombaugh spotted the moving point of light on plates taken at Lowell Observatory.

events.title: Structure of DNA published
events.description: Watson and Crick described the double helix in the journal Nature.

events.title: Penicillin discovered
events.description: Alexander Fleming noticed mould killing bacteria on a forgotten culture plate.

events.title: X-rays discovered
events.description: Wilhelm Röntgen observed a new kind of ray while experimenting with a cathode tube.

events.title: First powered aeroplane flight
events.description: The Wright brothers flew at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, for twelve seconds.

events.title: First telephone call
events.description: Alexander Graham Bell spoke the first words transmitted by telephone.

events.title: The World Wide Web proposed
events.description: Tim Berners-Lee circulated his proposal for an information management system at CERN.

events.title: The Web goes public
events.description: The first website outside CERN's internal network was made available to the world.

events.title: Large Hadron Collider switched on
events.description: The first proton beams circulated in the 27-kilometre ring near Geneva.

events.title: Higgs boson announced
events.description: CERN reported the discovery of a new particle consistent with the Higgs boson.

events.title: The Berlin Wall opens
events.description: East Germany allowed free passage, and crowds began dismantling the wall that night.

events.title: Nelson Mandela released
events.description: He walked free after 27 years in prison, four years before becoming president.

events.title: South Africa's first free election
events.description: Voters of all races queued together in the country's first democratic ballot.

events.title: India becomes independent
events.description: British rule ended at midnight, creating the modern states of India and Pakistan.

events.title: Victory in Europe Day
events.description: Germany's unconditional surrender ended the Second World War in Europe.

events.title: Atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima
events.description: The first use of a nuclear weapon in war destroyed most of the city.

events.title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
events.description: The United Nations General Assembly adopted the declaration in Paris.

events.title: "I Have a Dream"
events.description: Martin Luther King Jr. spoke to the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom.

events.title: Woodstock opens
events.description: Around 400,000 people gathered on a dairy farm in New York State for three days of music.

events.title: On the Origin of Species published
events.description: Charles Darwin set out the theory of evolution by natural selection.

events.title: Columbus reaches the Americas
events.description: His expedition made landfall in the Bahamas, beginning sustained contact across the Atlantic.

events.title: Storming of the Bastille
events.description: Parisians seized the fortress-prison, a turning point of the French Revolution.

events.title: Magna Carta sealed
events.description: King John accepted limits on royal power at Runnymede.

events.title: Emancipation Proclamation takes effect
events.description: Enslaved people in the rebelling American states were declared free.

events.title: Titanic sinks
events.description: The liner went down in the North Atlantic after striking an iceberg.

events.title: Tambora erupts
events.description: The largest eruption in recorded history led to the following "year without a summer".

events.title: Krakatoa erupts
events.description: The explosion was heard thousands of kilometres away and reddened skies worldwide for months.

events.title: Tunguska event
events.description: An air burst over Siberia flattened some 2,000 square kilometres of forest.

events.title: Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 hits Jupiter
events.description: Fragments of the comet began a week of impacts visible from Earth.

events.title: Chernobyl disaster
events.description: Reactor four exploded during a safety test, spreading fallout across Europe.

events.title: Battle of Waterloo
events.description: Napoleon's final defeat ended more than two decades of European war.

events.title: First message on ARPANET
events.description: The network that grew into the internet carried its first login attempt between two universities.

events.title: Battle of the Little Bighorn
events.description: Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho forces defeated the US 7th Cavalry in Montana.

events.title: Polio vaccine declared effective
events.description: Trial results for Jonas Salk's vaccine were announced to the public.

events.title: Smallpox declared eradicated
events.description: The World Health Assembly confirmed the end of the only human disease ever eradicated.

events.title: Human Genome Project completed
events.description: The consortium announced an essentially finished sequence of the human genome.

events.title: Dolly the sheep born
events.description: The first mammal cloned from an adult cell was born in Scotland.

events.title: Luna 2 reaches the Moon
events.description: The first spacecraft to touch another world hit the lunar surface.

events.title: First spacewalk
events.description: Alexei Leonov left his Voskhod 2 capsule for twelve minutes.

events.title: First space station launched
events.description: Salyut 1 began the era of long-duration crewed stations in orbit.

events.title: First module of the ISS launched
events.description: Zarya reached orbit, starting assembly of the International Space Station.

events.title: Voyager 1 launched
events.description: The probe went on to survey Jupiter and Saturn and to leave the Solar System.

events.title: Voyager 2 launched
events.description: The only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune began its grand tour.

events.title: Huygens lands on Titan
events.description: The probe descended through Titan's haze and photographed riverbeds of liquid methane.

events.title: Philae lands on a comet
events.description: The Rosetta lander made the first controlled touchdown on a comet nucleus.

events.title: Gravitational waves announced
events.description: LIGO reported detecting ripples in spacetime from two merging black holes.

events.title: Cosmic microwave background found
events.description: Penzias and Wilson traced a persistent hiss to the afterglow of the Big Bang.

events.title: First pulsar detected
events.description: Jocelyn Bell Burnell noticed a regular radio pulse from a spinning neutron star.

events.title: Eclipse confirms general relativity
events.description: Starlight bending around the eclipsed Sun matched Einstein's prediction.

events.title: Crab supernova recorded
events.description: Chinese astronomers logged a "guest star" bright enough to be seen in daylight.

events.title: Supernova 1987A seen
events.description: The nearest supernova in nearly four centuries appeared in the Large Magellanic Cloud.

events.title: Earth passes through Halley's tail
events.description: The planet crossed the comet's tail, prompting worldwide excitement and alarm.

events.title: Halley's Comet at perihelion
events.description: The comet made its closest approach to the Sun on its most recent visit.

events.title: Comet Hale-Bopp at perihelion
events.description: One of the brightest comets of the century was visible to the naked eye for months.

events.title: Last crewed Moon landing
events.description: Apollo 17 touched down in the Taurus-Littrow valley.

events.title: Apollo 13 oxygen tank explodes
events.description: An improvised rescue brought the crew home after the accident on the way to the Moon.

events.title: Earthrise photographed
events.description: Apollo 8's crew, the first to orbit the Moon, took one of the most reproduced pictures ever made.

events.title: First colour newspaper supplement
events.description: The New York World printed the first colour supplement in an American newspaper.

events.title: First public film screening
events.description: The Lumière brothers showed moving pictures to a paying audience in Paris.

events.title: Lindbergh lands in Paris
events.description: He completed the first solo non-stop flight across the Atlantic.

events.title: Amelia Earhart crosses the Atlantic
events.description: She became the first woman to fly the ocean solo, landing in Northern Ireland.

events.title: Everest summited
events.description: Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary reached the highest point on Earth.

events.title: Descent to the Challenger Deep
events.description: The bathyscaphe Trieste reached the deepest known point of the ocean.

events.title: South Pole reached
events.description: Roald Amundsen's party became the first to stand at the geographic South Pole.

events.title: Sesame Street premieres
events.description: The children's programme began a run that would reach audiences in more than 150 countries.

events.title: Live Aid
events.description: Concerts in London and Philadelphia were broadcast to an estimated 1.9 billion people.

events.title: Jesse Owens wins his fourth gold
events.description: His victories at the Berlin Olympics rebuked the Nazi ideology of the host state.

events.title: First modern Olympic Games
events.description: The games opened in Athens with athletes from fourteen nations.

events.title: The Salt March begins
events.description: Gandhi set out for the sea to make salt in defiance of British law.

events.title: People's Republic of China founded
events.description: Mao Zedong proclaimed the new state from Tiananmen Gate.

events.title: Treaty of Rome signed
events.description: Six countries created the European Economic Community, forerunner of the EU.

events.title: The Soviet Union dissolves
events.description: The Supreme Soviet formally voted the union out of existence.

events.title: Attacks on the United States
events.description: Coordinated hijackings killed nearly 3,000 people and reshaped global politics.

events.title: Paris climate agreement adopted
events.description: 195 countries agreed to limit global warming to well below two degrees.

events.title: COVID-19 declared a pandemic
events.description: The World Health Organization applied the term as the outbreak spread worldwide.

events.title: Stonewall uprising
events.description: Protests in New York became a catalyst for the modern gay rights movement.

events.title: New Zealand grants women the vote
events.description: It became the first self-governing country where women could vote in national elections.

events.title: First woman in space
events.description: Valentina Tereshkova spent almost three days in orbit aboard Vostok 6.

events.title: Sally Ride reaches orbit
events.description: She became the first American woman in space aboard Challenger.

events.title: First liquid-fuelled rocket
events.description: Robert Goddard's rocket flew for two and a half seconds in Massachusetts.

events.title: First rocket to reach space
events.description: A German A-4 test flight crossed the boundary of space for the first time.

events.title: Van Gogh paints in Arles
events.description: His Provençal period produced The Starry Night Over the Rhône among other works.

events.title: Eiffel Tower completed
events.description: The tower opened as the entrance arch of the Paris World's Fair.

events.title: Bombing of Guernica
events.description: The attack on the Basque town inspired Picasso's mural of the same name.

events.title: Tutankhamun's tomb found
events.description: Howard Carter uncovered the step leading to the almost intact royal tomb.

events.title: Rosetta Stone found
events.description: The slab that unlocked Egyptian hieroglyphs was uncovered near Rashid.

events.title: Terracotta Army discovered
events.description: Farmers digging a well in Shaanxi struck the buried army of China's first emperor.

events.title: Printing with movable type in Europe
events.description: Gutenberg's workshop in Mainz began the experiments that led to the printing press.

events.title: The Beatles' rooftop concert
events.description: The band played their last public performance on a London roof.

events.title: Sound film spreads worldwide
events.description: The success of talking pictures ended the silent era within two years.

events.title: First microprocessor sold
events.description: Intel released the 4004, putting a computer's processor on a single chip.

events.title: First Macintosh goes on sale
events.description: The computer brought the graphical interface and mouse to a mass market.

events.title: The iPhone announced
events.description: The launch reshaped mobile computing and the software industry around it.

events.title: First four-minute mile
events.description: Roger Bannister ran the distance in 3 minutes 59.4 seconds at Oxford.

events.title: England win the World Cup
events.description: The hosts beat West Germany 4-2 after extra time at Wembley.

events.title: Brazil win a third World Cup
events.description: Pelé's side beat Italy 4-1 in Mexico City and kept the Jules Rimet trophy.

events.title: India win the Cricket World Cup
events.description: India beat the West Indies at Lord's and transformed the sport at home.

events.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis peaks
events.description: Vasili Arkhipov's refusal to approve a nuclear torpedo helped avert war.

events.title: SALT I signed
events.description: The first strategic arms limitation agreement capped nuclear missile launchers.

events.title: Montreal Protocol signed
events.description: Nations agreed to phase out the chemicals destroying the ozone layer.

events.title: Antarctic ozone hole reported
events.description: British Antarctic Survey scientists published evidence of severe seasonal ozone loss.

events.title: "Ich bin ein Berliner"
events.description: President Kennedy addressed a vast crowd in West Berlin.

events.title: Star Trek premieres
events.description: The series began its influence on generations of scientists and engineers.

events.title: Star Wars released
events.description: The film opened in a handful of American cinemas and became a global phenomenon.

events.title: Iraq invades Kuwait
events.description: The invasion led to the first Gulf War and a decade of sanctions.

events.title: Indian Ocean tsunami
events.description: A magnitude 9.1 earthquake off Sumatra caused waves that killed some 230,000 people.

events.title: San Francisco earthquake
events.description: The quake and the fires that followed destroyed most of the city.

events.title: Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami
events.description: Japan's largest recorded earthquake triggered the Fukushima nuclear accident.

events.title: The Great Smog of London
events.description: Five days of lethal smog led to the first Clean Air Act.

events.title: The Carrington Event
events.description: The strongest recorded solar storm set telegraph lines sparking and lit aurorae near the tropics.

events.title: Quebec blackout by solar storm
events.description: A geomagnetic storm knocked out power to six million people for nine hours.
